name: Concord
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Concord, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Concord, MA: Holiday Pops at Umbrella Arts, the Concord Band with Nutcracker dancers, family art days and the town tree lighting.
lede: Concord does Christmas through its arts and its history: a tree lighting in Monument Square with Santa on a fire truck, holiday concerts that go back to 1976, and story trees at the Concord Museum.
celebrates: Concord Recreation runs the town's Annual Tree Lighting in Monument Square on an early December Sunday, with a parade from the Hunt, music on a main stage, food trucks and Santa photos. The Umbrella Arts Center on Stow Street fills December with a Winter Market, free family art afternoons, Holiday Handcraft Days and a Holiday Pops concert. The Concord Band has played its own Holiday Pops since 1976. The Concord Museum turns its galleries into Family Trees, story trees decorated after picture books, and Louisa May Alcott's Orchard House holds A Dickensian Christmas with living history portrayers, Victorian music, games and crafts.
lastyear: Concord's Annual Tree Lighting was held on Sunday, December 7, 2025, in Monument Square. Concord Recreation's schedule closed the roads at 3 pm for vendors and food trucks, with The Concord Players on the main stage, a Presbyterian Church performance, a clarinet choir and a sax quartet from 51 Walden, and the CMS Band. The parade stepped off from the Hunt at 4:30 pm, the tree was lit at 5:10 pm, and Santa photos at the Holy Family Parish Center and a holiday sing-along followed.
facts: Family Trees: A Celebration of Children's Literature has filled the Concord Museum each holiday season for more than 30 years, and the museum marked its 30th year with a birthday party. Each tree is decorated by local volunteers after a picture book. Orchard House, where Louisa May Alcott lived, calls itself the home of Little Women. The Concord Band's Holiday Pops dates to 1976, and the Winter Market at Umbrella Arts has been a Concord tradition for twenty years.
trains: Concord has two stations on the MBTA Fitchburg Line, Concord and West Concord. Inbound trains run through Lincoln, Waltham, Belmont and Porter to North Station in Boston, so a holiday trip into the city does not need a car, and outbound trains continue to South Acton, Littleton and Fitchburg. For a train ride with a holiday theme, Edaville in Carver runs a Holiday Express through Christmas lights, and Lowell has the Boston and Maine Railroad Historical Society's steam locomotive No. 410 and the National Streetcar Museum.

faq: When is the Concord tree lighting?

Concord Recreation holds the Annual Tree Lighting in Monument Square on a Sunday in early December. In 2025 it was December 7, with vendors and food trucks from 3 pm, a parade from the Hunt at 4:30 pm, the lighting at 5:10 pm and Santa photos at the Holy Family Parish Center afterward. Roads in the center close for the afternoon.
What is Family Trees at the Concord Museum?

Family Trees: A Celebration of Children's Literature is the Concord Museum's holiday installation. Local volunteers and community groups decorate dozens of story trees, each after a beloved picture book. Families walk through the display, read together and follow a scavenger hunt, and the museum adds an afternoon to meet local authors and illustrators. Museum members get in free.
Is there a holiday concert for kids in Concord?

Yes, more than one. The Umbrella Arts Center hosts the Firebird Pops Orchestra's Holiday Pops with drop-in art activities for elementary age kids and a sing-along finale. The Concord Band has played its own Holiday Pops, with audience sing-alongs, since 1976. Both concerts sell lower priced tickets for children.
What is A Dickensian Christmas at Orchard House?

It is a living history program at Louisa May Alcott's Orchard House on Lexington Road. Portrayers, Victorian music, games and crafts bring an Alcott family Christmas to life in the decorated rooms. Orchard House calls it a perennially popular event, strongly urges reservations, and uses it to support its education and preservation work.
Can we take the train to Concord?

Yes. Concord has two stops on the MBTA Fitchburg Line, Concord and West Concord. Inbound trains continue through Lincoln, Waltham, Belmont and Porter to North Station in Boston, and outbound trains head on to South Acton, Littleton and Fitchburg. Check the MBTA weekend schedule before planning a holiday trip by train.
